pages.title: Champion ability
pages.content:
: {{Hatnote|''Also see: [[List of abilities|List of all abilities]].''}} A '''champion ability''' is a type of [[Terminology#Spell|spell]], or move, that is uniquely available to a certain [[champion]]. The entire set of a champion's abilities is commonly referred to as their ''kit''. == Terminology == Champion abilities are a category of spells, and spells are ''[[Passive and active spell|cast]]'' (activated) in one of two ways, ''passively'' or ''actively''. This refers to the level of player input required. Each champion ability may feature any number of passive and/or active effects. Because the order of champion abilities on the player's HUD is immutable (unlike the [[inventory]] and [[summoner spell]] loadouts), champion abilities are distinguished by and can be referred to using the name of their ''key slot'' instead of their title, meaning the order on the player's HUD and its corresponding key. Those key slots are: I / [[File:Q.png|20px|border|link=|Q ability slot icon]] / [[File:W.png|20px|border|link=|W ability slot icon]] / [[File:E.png|20px|border|link=|E ability slot icon]] / [[File:R.png|20px|border|link=|R ability slot icon]] == Kit == All of a champion's abilities together is called their '''kit'''. Most champions' '''kit''' follows a similar structure. An innate ability, a number of basic abilities—typically three—and an ultimate ability. Each ability may grant a number of effects or even have different behaviors. * {{sbc|Innate:}} An ''innate'' ability is learned as soon as the game starts and cannot be improved via skill points. All champions have one innate ability available that defines their play style or strategy. * {{sbc|Basic ability:}} A ''basic ability'' is part of a champion's common and repeatable move set. * {{sbc|Ultimate:}} The ''ultimate'' ability is a champion's signature ability. It involves high-potency effects that can change the game. * {{sbc|Pseudo-Ultimate}}: A ''pseudo-ultimate'' is an ability classified as an ultimate for effects that interact with ultimate abilities ("ultimate effects"), such as {{cai|Hijack|Sylas}} and {{ri|Axiom Arcanist}}, but deviates greatly from the typical design. This includes transforming champions' transformation ability, low-cooldown abilities like {{cai|Portal Jump|Zoe}}, as well as abilities that upgrade other abilities to new ones upon casting the pseudo-ultimate. A circle next to champions in the scoreboard portraits represents their ultimate/R slot, which can be [[ping]]ed to display various information in [[chat]]. For allies, who are also shown in the portraits at the edge of the player's screen, the circle also displays the status of their ultimate, and the exact cooldown is shown to the team whenever pinged. If the ally's ultimate/R slot is on cooldown, the circle fills up radially as the cooldown elapses. The circle is black while the respective ability has not been learned, blue while counting its cooldown, and green while the ability is available. == List of abilities == For a page listing all Champion abilities, see below:

Main article: [[List of abilities]]

== Skill Points == No champion has their entire kit available at once and at its full potency right from the start of a game. For this purpose, '''skill points''' exist that players can obtain and spend (allocate) in ''learning'' and ''ranking'' their preferred abilities. An ability becomes immediately available to use upon learning it (conditions to cast a component must still be fulfilled). Each ability slot can have a maximum number of skill points that players can spend on, strictly from zero to six. * Innate abilities cannot be ranked up via skill points. * Basic abilities usually have five ranks at most. * Ultimate abilities usually have three ranks at most. Abilities can be referred to by the number of skill points spent on them, with unlearned abilities being considered rank zero. Ability ranks are denoted via the number of ranks before their slot letter (e.g. 3Q means the Q slot at rank 3). Abilities at rank zero that grant a passive effect corresponding to another ability may affect the latter at a different potency. Examples include: * {{cai|Searing Brilliance|Mel|Overwhelm}} stored damage is increased with each rank in {{ai|Golden Eclipse|Mel}}. * {{cai|Across the Veil|Aurora}} ''Realm Hopper'' {{sti|ms|movement speed}} is increased with each rank in the ability but it is also granted by {{ai|Between Worlds|Aurora}}. === Obtaining skill points === One skill point is obtained each time the champion {{stil|xp|levels up}}, with the first being granted at level 1 always, and a maximum of 18 possible from leveling up. One additional skill point can be obtained by consuming {{ii|Elixir of Skill}}, a distributed item. This is always true in all game modes, as the number of an ability's ranks cannot change. === Spending skill points === While available, skill points can be spent by clicking on the corresponding arrow in the grid above the respective slot in the HUD, or using the respective [[hotkeys]] (default: {{sbc|Ctrl}} + {{sbc|Q}} / {{sbc|Ctrl}} + {{sbc|W}} / {{sbc|Ctrl}} + {{sbc|E}} / {{sbc|Ctrl}} + {{sbc|R}}). Note that the same grid and leveling system is used for {{cai|Glorious Evolution|Viktor}} ''augments'', though it is independent of and takes precedence over ability ranking, and that {{ci|Hwei}} is forbidden from spending skill points while in any of his three moods even while he has skill points available. === Ranking order & rules === The order in which a player spends skill points in each ability slot as they are obtained is referred to as their ''skill order''. However, there are certain rules that the game enforces on ''skill order'' for game balance purposes, in order to render matches more uniform and intuitive, and to incentivize players to employ their entire kit. * The first skill point can be spent on any '''basic''' ability. ** {{cai|Burst Fire|Zeri}} is uniquely learned at the start of the game automatically, with the first skill point being expended. ** {{ci|Azir}} must rank {{ai|Arise!|Azir}} as his first ability, and will do so automatically if he reaches level 2 before ranking an ability. ** {{cai|You and Me!|Yuumi}}, as well as certain pseudo-ultimate abilities that correspond to the R slot are already learned at the start of the game, but the first skill point is still available for ranking a basic ability. * Beyond level 1, the current rank of any ability cannot exceed half the champion's current level rounded down. This rule practically limits each new rank for the same ability to every odd, single-digit level. * Ultimate abilities can only be learned/ranked upon reaching levels 6, 11, 16. Skill order is denoted by typing out each slot's letter that the player spends each skill point on in succession, without any spaces: e.g. EQWEQRE… The order in which a player maxes out the ranks of their abilities as soon as ranking them becomes available is referred to as their ''max order''. Since ultimate abilities are very potent and thus players are generally always incentivized to learn and rank them up as they become available, the ultimate ability (R slot) tends to be omitted when referring to the max order. Common conventions for notation include e.g. "E > Q > W" and permutations of such. Certain champions are required to learn certain abilities to use some others. This includes: * {{cai|Conquering Sands|Azir}} and {{ai|Shifting Sands|Azir}} require {{ai|Arise!|Azir}}. * {{cai|Spirit's Refuge|Shen}} requires {{ai|Twilight Assault|Shen}}. * {{cai|Bladecaller|Xayah}} requires either {{ai|Double Daggers|Xayah}} or {{ai|Deadly Plumage|Xayah}}. * {{cai|Rewind|Zilean}} requires either {{ai|Time Bomb|Zilean}} or {{ai|Time Warp|Zilean}}. * {{cai|Rampant Growth|Zyra}} requires either {{ai|Deadly Spines|Zyra}} or {{ai|Grasping Roots|Zyra}}. == Components == : ''Any given ability can possess one or more of the following components (combinations may vary)'' * {{sbc|Scaling:}} Abilities increase in potency and/or strength through a portion of certain [[Champion statistic|stats]] that the champion has acquired, such as from [[item]]s and/or [[rune]]s. * {{sbc|Cost:}} Most abilities require the champion to expend a [[Ability resource|resource]] cost ({{sti|mana|link=true}}, {{sti|energy|link=true}}, {{sti|health|link=true}} or other) in order to be cast, becoming unable to do so if they possess less than the required amount (the ability's HUD icon will turn blue). ** Toggles continuously consume a resource until the ability is toggled off manually or does so automatically upon resource depletion. ** Resourceless champions do not have costs on their abilities. * {{sbc|Cooldown:}} Champions must wait a certain length of time before they can use the same ability again via a {{sti|cooldown|link=true}}. This wait can be shortened by the [[haste]] stat. * {{sbc|[[Ammunition|Ammo]]:}} Some abilities run on charges (as opposed to a cooldown) in order to be used. ** '''Stock:''' Activation charges are generated periodically up to a maximum (recharge time is affected by ability haste) ** '''Barrage:''' Charges are generated upon activating the ability, and are available for the duration (all unused charges are lost when it ends). Used charges incur no additional resource costs, but are gated with static recast cooldowns. * {{sbc|[[Range]]:}} Describes the number of units the caster and the target must be from one another in order for the ability to be cast / to hit (hitbox collision detection determines if the range used is {{tip|center range|center-based}} or {{tip|edge range|edge-based}}). ** In-game tooltips do not display either range or targeting (visually drawn by placing the cursor over an ability's icon on the HUD) ** Some abilities feature an unlimited global range, commonly ultimates. * {{sbc|[[Cast time]]:}} Abilities may incur a casting time in which the champion is unable to perform any other actions for a short period of time until the ability takes effect (can only be interrupted by the champion's [[death]]). Cast times are measured in seconds and commonly last for {{fd|0.25}}, {{fd|0.5}}, and 1 second(s). They prevent abilities from triggering their effects instantaneously. ** A cast may include a ''lockout'' that prevents certain actives until afterward (buffer), or disables them entirely. This lockout can extend past the cast time up until the ability ends. * {{sbc|[[Channel]]:}} Abilities may incur a channeling time in which the champion is either unable to or must not perform any other actions for a period of time in order for the ability to successfully take effect during the time of the channel or after it completes. Channels can be interrupted by the caster themselves by performing certain actions that would do so (unless otherwise stated) and all forms of {{tip|cast-inhibiting crowd control}} in addition to {{tip|disrupt}}. ** A special form of channel includes charged abilities, where the caster must maintain their channel in order to increase the ability's effectiveness over the duration. These abilities have both an active and a recast component. * {{sbc|Stance:}} Causes the champion to ''shapeshift'' themselves and/or their abilities, gaining persistent effects (mutually exclusive) and/or temporary ones while losing others. ** Rapid stance-swapping is usually regulated by a brief global cooldown in order to prevent a champion from continually accumulating temporary effects. ** Some stances replace temporary effects by granting completely different basic abilities based on the active stance. * {{sbc|[[Champion summoned units|Summon]]:}} Champions can bring forth other units to assist them and/or their allies on the battlefield. * {{sbc|[[On-Action Effects]]:}} Abilities within a champion's kit can interact with certain actions and/or each other for synergistic effects and results. ** Most abilities apply [[spell vamp]], [[omnivamp]] and/or [[spell effects]] from items and runes. *** A select few apply [[on-hit effect]]s and [[on-attack effect]]s (but only if specifically stated to be able to do so). == Effects == : ''Any given ability can possess one or more of the following effects (combinations may vary)'' * {{sbc|Combat:}} Enhances offensive and/or defensive aspects. ** [[Damage]] allows champions to kill enemy units. ** [[Buff]]s affect the caster and/or their allies for their benefit. ** [[Debuff]]s affect the caster's enemies for their detriment. *** [[Crowd control]] is a special, standardized category of debuffs which temporarily disable certain actions enemies are allowed to perform or hinder other capabilities. * {{sbc|Utility:}} Enhances non-combat aspects. ** {{tip|Blink|Blinks}}, {{tip|dash|dashes}}, {{sti|ms|hastes}} and {{tip|ghosting}} effects serve as forms of mobility for a champion, allowing them to reposition, move around obstacles, or close the gap to and create distance from their opponents. ** {{tip|Heal|Healing}} provides a means of remaining in combat longer. ** {{tip|Shield|Shields}} enhance survivability by absorbing damage to prevent health loss. ** {{tip|Stealth}} grants {{tip|invisibility}} and {{tip|camouflage}} to avoid enemy detection. ** {{tip|Invulnerability}} gives immunity to sources of enemy damage. ** {{tip|Untargetability}} grants immunity to enemy focus-fire (preventing targeted abilities from acquiring a unit as a target) == Trivia == === General === * {{ci|Hwei}} is currently the champion with the highest number of abilities in the game: 11 when excluding his subject selection spells, and 15 when including them. * {{ai|Spider Form|Elise}} / {{ai|Human Form|Elise}}, {{ai|Rage Gene|Gnar}}, {{ai|Transform Mercury Hammer|Jayce|Mercury Hammer}} / {{ai|Transform Mercury Cannon|Jayce|Mercury Cannon}}, {{ai|The Darkin Scythe|Kayn}}, {{ai|Skaarl the Cowardly Lizard|Kled}}, {{ai|Aspect of the Cougar|Nidalee}}, {{ai|Behind Enemy Lines|Quinn}} / {{ai|Skystrike|Quinn}}, and {{ai|Burrow|Rek'Sai}} / {{ai|Unburrow|Rek'Sai}}, are stance abilities that 'shapeshift' their wielders, granting them one or more extra basic abilities. === Innate abilities === * {{ai|Moonsilver Blade|Diana}}, {{ai|Nimble Fighter|Fizz}}, {{ai|Searing Brilliance|Mel}}, {{ai|Darkness Rise|Mordekaiser}}, {{ai|Living Forge|Ornn}}, {{ai|Pit Grit|Sett}}, {{ai|Crimson Pact|Vladimir}}, {{ai|Way of the Wanderer|Yasuo}}, {{ai|Way of the Hunter|Yone}} and {{ai|Cell Division|Zac}} are innate abilities featuring two or more independent effects. * {{ai|Spider Queen|Elise}} and {{ai|Aspect of the Cougar|Nidalee}} are the only innate abilities with two effects that stack with others and/or with abilities. * {{ai|Death Defied|Karthus}}, {{ai|Icathian Surprise|Kog'Maw}}, and {{ai|Glory in Death|Sion}} are the only innate abilities that allow for post-{{tip|death}} activity. * {{ai|Shurima's Legacy|Azir}}, {{ai|Prophet of an Elder God|Illaoi}} and {{ai|Garden of Thorns|Zyra}} are the only summon innate abilities. * {{ai|Rage Gene|Gnar}}, {{ai|The Darkin Scythe|Kayn}}, and {{ai|Skaarl the Cowardly Lizard|Kled}} are the only stance innate abilities. * {{ai|A Harmless Scarecrow|Fiddlesticks}} is currently the only ability preventing the user from purchasing an item. * {{ai|Martial Poise|Kalista}} is the only ability that generates a unique item for the user. * {{ai|Transcendent|Syndra}} has the most independent effects of any ability (four). === Basic abilities === * {{cis|Jayce}} and {{cis|Udyr}} basic abilities can have six ranks. ** {{cis|Udyr}} ultimate ability is also uniquely tied to his innate, which has a pseudo-ultimate component (''Awakened Spirit''). ** {{cai|Prowling Projectile|Yuumi}} can individually have six ranks. * All of {{cis|Lee Sin}} basic ability slots correspond to two distinct abilities. * {{ci|Kha'Zix}} and {{ci|Viktor}} are the only champions that can permanently evolve their abilities throughout the game. ** {{ci|Kai'Sa}} and {{ci|Syndra}} gain extra permanent effects on all of their abilities. ** {{ci|Rengar}} gains extra temporary effects on all of his basic abilities. ** {{ai|The Darkin Scythe|Kayn}} and {{ai|Dragon's Descent|Shyvana}} 'shapeshift' both their wielders and basic abilities. ** {{ai|The Darkin Scythe|Kayn}} allows only a single stance change per game. * {{cai|Weapon Queue System|Aphelios}}, set to his E slot, is the only ability in the game to have no gameplay effect. ** This transcends the definition of ability and therefore the button should not be called an ability. Nevertheless it remains a slot in his kit and its effect is internally coded as an ability-sourced buff due to the way the engine works. === Ultimate abilities === * {{cis|Nocturne}}, {{cis|Kayn}}, {{cis|Ornn}}, {{cis|Quinn}}, {{cis|Riven}}, {{cis|Tahm Kench}}, {{cis|Twisted Fate}}, and {{cis|Urgot}} ultimate abilities each have two differing casts within a single ability usage. ** This excludes ultimates that are repeatable, toggleable or terminable by their second cast. * {{ai|Enchanted Crystal Arrow|Ashe}}, {{ai|Whirling Death|Draven}}, {{ai|Chronobreak|Ekko}}, {{ai|Trueshot Barrage|Ezreal}}, {{ai|Cannon Barrage|Gangplank}}, {{ai|Super Mega Death Rocket!|Jinx}}, {{ai|Requiem|Karthus}}, {{ai|Lilting Lullaby|Lillia}}, {{ai|Golden Eclipse|Mel}}, {{ais|Paranoia|Nocturne}} {{tip|nearsight}}, {{ai|Dawning Shadow|Senna}}, {{ai|Stand United|Shen}}, {{ai|Wish|Soraka}}, and {{ai|Destiny|Twisted Fate}}'s {{tip|true sight|reveal}} are the only global ultimate abilities. * {{ai|Spider Form|Elise}} / {{ai|Human Form|Elise}}, {{ai|Mantra|Karma}} and {{ai|Aspect of the Cougar|Nidalee}} are all available at level 1 and each has four ranks (levels 1, 6, 11, and 16). ** {{ai|Transform Mercury Hammer|Jayce|Mercury Hammer}} / {{ai|Transform Mercury Cannon|Jayce|Mercury Cannon}} is available at level 1 and has only one rank. * {{ai|Endless Banquet|Bel'Veth}} is the only ultimate ability that evolves a champion into a different form and grants extra stats. ==== Pseudo-Ultimate abilities ==== * {{cai|Wingborne Storm|Udyr}} * {{cai|Transform Mercury Hammer|Jayce}} / {{ai|Transform Mercury Cannon|Jayce}} === Others === * {{ai|Riposte|Fiora}}, {{ai|Divine Judgment|Kayle}}, and {{ai|Cosmic Radiance|Taric}} are the only abilities that provide pure [[invulnerability]]. ** {{ai|Tempered Fate|Bard}}, {{ai|Frozen Tomb|Lissandra}}, {{ai|Force of Will|Syndra}} (non-champions only), and {{ai|Chronoshift|Zilean}} grant invulnerability through {{tip|stasis}} effect. ** {{ai|Hallowed Mist|Gwen}}, {{ai|Crescent Guard|Xin Zhao}}, {{ai|Lamb's Respite|Kindred}}, and {{ai|Aegis Assault|Pantheon}} have a conditional [[invulnerability]]. {{ci|Gwen}} and {{ci|Xin Zhao}} are vulnerable if enemies enter their respective zones; {{ci|Kindred}} and allied champs can be displaced outside of {{ai|Lamb's Respite|Kindred}} and lose the invulnerability. {{ci|Pantheon}} is only invulnerable in the direction he faces with his shield. == Non-Champion Abilities == Epic [[monster]]s, such as {{ui|Baron Nashor}} and {{ui|Dragon|Elemental Drakes}}, as well as the {{ui|Rift Herald|Mercenary}}, generally have one to a few unique active or passive abilities available that are distinct from champion abilities. The offensive abilities of those monsters may interact with and break champion {{tip|spell shield|spell shields}}. All other non-champion units have permanently available effects that are handled purely by the game rules instead of through a specific ability. Some units have no set of moves at all including [[basic attack]]s (e.g. [[jungle plants]] and some types of [[ward]]s). Non-champion units may have a pseudo-inventory that can be viewed in their target frame upon [[Unit selection|focusing]] them (default: {{LMB}} MB1 / left-click) which may explain some of their behavior or effects. {{References}} == See Also == {{Gameplay elements}} [[de:Fähigkeiten]] [[es:Habilidad de campeón]] [[fr:Compétence]] [[pl:Umiejętność]] [[pt-br:Habilidade]] [[ru:Умение чемпиона]] [[zh:英雄技能]] [[Category:Gameplay elements]] [[Category:Abilities]] [[Category:Champions]]

== Notes ==
* '''Coup de Grace''' only triggers on damage dealt after the champion is brought {{as|below 40% health}}.

== Trivia ==
* '''Coup de Grace''' is a French {{w|Coup de grâce|phrase}} that literally translates to "stroke of grace" or "blow of mercy", a final strike on one that is mortally wounded. It effectively means "knockout", "lethal blow", "killing stroke" or "deathblow".

pages.title: Damage
pages.content:
{{ToDo|This article and the '''Damage types''' section in particular contain confusing or outdated information that is presently subject to a complete overhaul.}} : {{hatnote|''Not to be confused with [[attack damage]], a champion statistic, nor conflated with [[Health#Health as a casting resource|health costs]], which are not damage.''}} [[File:Damage Annie.png|thumb|200px|Damage is displayed as a red section on a champion's health bar.]] '''Damage''' is the result of a direct [[combat]] interaction between two units: a source [[unit]] causes a deduction of a target unit's current [[health]] via a ''damaging'' [[spell]] (or accompanying [[debuff]]). Damage takes place in [[Tick and updates|engine time]] ("instantaneously") and the application itself is formally called a '''damage instance''' or '''damage event'''. {{tip|Invulnerability}} prevents damage, and {{tip|shield|shields}} can protect from it. Damage values can also be modified by the source or the target through [[damage modifier]]s. They can also be increased by a percentage due to an event called a {{tip|critical strike}}. Enemies are [[kill|slain]] upon dealing enough '''damage''' to deplete their [[health]]. A champion dealing damage against another champion triggers kill attribution (if it does not slay them otherwise) and, if the damage-dealer is within enemy {{tip|turret}} attack range, also triggers the turret's aggression until they exit the turret's range. == Types == The following three '''damage types''' exist: {{as|{{sbc|Physical}}|physical damage}}, {{as|{{sbc|Magic}}|magic damage}}, and {{as|{{sbc|True}}|true damage}}. Each damage event can fall under only one of these three categories. These three types exist to add variability to gameplay beyond simple deduction of health equal to the source's outgoing damage value, by potentially reducing, or '''''mitigating''''' it instead. * {{as|Physical damage}} is innately mitigated by {{stil|armor}}, a statistic that units possess. * {{as|Magic damage}} is innately mitigated by {{stil|magic resistance}}, a statistic that units possess. * {{as|True damage}} cannot be mitigated by any innate statistic. Aside from these innate mitigations, various effects can also reduce outgoing damage by a source (e.g. {{si|Exhaust}}), reduce incoming damage from all or some sources (e.g. {{cai|Meditate|Master Yi}}), potentially nullify any damage received (e.g. {{tip|invulnerability}}) or prevent an effect, which may or may not be accompanied by damage, from being applied altogether (e.g. {{tip|spell shield}}). {{as|True damage}} additionally has the property of being largely unaffected by damage ''reductions'', with the exception of {{cai|Riposte|Fiora}}, which invariably reduces all incoming non-{{tip|execute|execution}} damage dealt by sources other than {{tip|turrets}} by 100%. Effects that trigger from damage '''type''' will always occur, unless prevented from applying altogether, regardless of its classification. == Additional classification == In addition to types, damage instances can have multiple other classifications to determine and manage interactions systemically. Note that damage instances can equal zero (i.e. a health deduction, of zero). This is most commonly utilized for triggering [[kill]] attribution and minion aggression. === Tags === The '''tag''' system is a restrictive classification applicable to the ''source'' of the damage instance. It is restrictive because each tag entails a number of default ''properties'' the damage instance can have, and spells that interact with other spells can choose to ignore certain tags. Damage instances can have any combination of these '''tags''', though some combinations are atypical or never found in game. Properties are a secondary classification system, explained further below. * '''BasicAttack:'''The {{SITENAME}} elected to call this 'basic damage' and avoid using the term 'attack' in order to prevent confusion between the damage type, the action, and the [[attack damage]] statistic. Represents the base damage of all champion [[basic attack]]s (invariably), most empowered attacks (e.g. {{cai|Power Fist|Blitzcrank}}, {{cai|Crippling Strike|Darius}}), most attack-like abilities/also referred to as attack-spells (e.g. {{cai|Mystic Shot|Ezreal}}, {{cai|Lunge|Fiora}}) and all attack modifiers (e.g. {{cai|Heroic Swing|Akshan}}, {{cai|Royal Maelstrom|Bel'Veth}}, {{cai|Purge|Urgot}}, {{iis|Runaan's Hurricane}} {{nie|Wind's Fury}} bolts). ** All champion basic attacks, which are tagged with this, apply {{stil|life steal}} and {{tip|on-hit|on-hit effects}} through the ApplyLifesteal and TriggerOnHitEvents properties, respectively, as a fundamental mechanic. However other damage tags can have these properties, meaning they are not exclusive to this tag. * '''ActiveSpell:''' Represents most [[active]] [[champion ability|champion]] and [[active ability items|item abilities]], i.e., ones that the player has issued an active command, and paid a cost if applicable, to cast. ** This tag allows triggering {{tip|ability effects}} (invariably). * '''AOE:''' Represents damage in an area ('''A'''rea '''o'''f '''E'''ffect) or sometimes across multiple units. ** This tag is usually tied to penalties compared to other damage tags, since area effects are considered easier to apply than single-target effects. * '''Periodic:''' Represents effects repeating at a cadence generally shorter than traditional [[cooldown]]s and over a period, instead of at once. The repetition can originate from a continually firing spell (e.g. {{cai|The Culling|Lucian}}, {{cai|Tormented Shadow|Morgana}}) or be applied via a debuff (e.g. {{cai|Malefic Visions|Malzahar}}, {{cai|Poison Trail|Singed}}, {{iis|Liandry's Torment}} {{nie|Torment}}). ** This tag is usually tied to even stricter penalties compared to AOE and additionally has the property of not expunging {{tip|sleep}}. * '''Proc:'''The term 'proc' refers to a mechanic that has a chance of triggering, which is common in games such as World of Warcraft (e.g., "Your attacks have an x % chance to cause [...]" effects). League of Legends originally featured 'true' proc effects (e.g., "your attacks have a chance to slow.") However, the design philosophy of Riot Games' over-time grew more towards preferring 'on-hit' or "every nth attack" to purely random mechanics. Despite this: the engine-level label persisted. The term 'proc' now describes all additional effect triggers even if they are not guaranteed, 'proc' is used as a verb when triggering such an effect. Represents all effects applied as secondary on top of other more interactive effects. This is used for any damage that should not trigger a chain of additional [[attack effects|attack]] and [[spell effects|spell effects]] due to other damage tags on a target. {{tip|On-hit}} and {{tip|spell effects}} themselves are usually tagged proc. ** This tag is self-limiting; it exists so that effects that trigger from other damage tags do not continuously apply and/or repeat. * '''Indirect:''' Represents effects that are to be considered "not actively or directly sourced by the player themselves". ** In addition to not expunging {{tip|sleep}} like Periodic, and being self-limiting like Proc, this tag is reserved for use in other systems that require exclusion of all other damage types. It is rare and any further uses as of [[2026 Annual Cycle|2026]] are {{tt|unknown|This used to interact with pre-rework Neeko disguise.}}. * '''Pet:''' Represents all damage originating from [[champion summoned units]], also to defer attribution to their summoner. * '''Item:''' Represents damage originating from most non-champion spells. Despite the name, this includes [[summoner spell]] damage against champions, in addition to [[item]] abilities. ** This tag is generally exclusionary; it exists so that non-champion-sourced damage is identified and grouped separately from other champion-sourced damage, as a lesser category, and so that it does not remain untagged, for consistency. Damage instances which are supposed to remain unaffected by effects that modify champion attacks or ability damage are also tagged as such. * '''NonRedirectable:''' Represents all damage that manipulates the source of the instance. It has no current known applications, except (presumably) {{cais|Sleepy Trouble Bubble|Zoe}} expunging of {{tip|sleep}} specifically. It may be vestigial. * '''DoesNotAggroJungle:''' Represents all damage that should not trigger neutral {{tip|monster}} aggression, which includes {{cai|Friend of the Forest|Ivern}} and the regular damage of {{ii|Gustwalker Hatchling|icononly=true}}{{ii|Mosstomper Seedling|icononly=true}}{{ii|Scorchclaw Pup|icononly=true}} [[jungle]] companions. * '''OnHit:''' Represents all {{tip|on-hit|on-hit effects}} (invariably). ** This tag exists for interaction with effects that modify and/or repeat on-hit effect application. * '''Augment:''' Represents damage dealt by [[augment]] systems in modes such as {{tip|Arena}} and {{tip|ARAM: Mayhem}} (invariably). ** This tag exists for interaction with effects that modify and/or repeat augment effect application. The same origin spell can have any number of damage instances, even occurring simultaneously. It can also apply different damage instances with different tags depending on the target, or even the number of targets hit (the latter includes effects such as {{cai|Lay Waste|Karthus}}). In addition to all of the above, damage can be made to ignore {{tip|shield|shields}} and other forms of health manipulation internally. This is not handled by any known tags or properties. It is however most relevant for damage that does not fall under any tag. === Untagged === Untagged damaging effects also exist, which can have completely custom properties, though they are rare. Crit multiplier explanation
* For a 175% (1.75x) crit multiplier, this 'some percent' damage increase is 75% (Add 0.75x base damage)
* For a 200% (2.00x) crit multiplier, this 'some percent' damage increase is 100% (Add 1.00x base damage)
* For a 230% (2.30x) crit multiplier, this 'some percent' damage increase is 130% (Add 1.30x base damage)
* For a CritMod (?.??x) crit multiplier, this 'some percent' damage increase is (CritMod% - 100%) (Add [CritMod - 1.00]x base damage) Some abilities or characters have a crit multiplier attached to them also. (e.g {{cai|Way of the Wanderer|Yasuo}}) Simply multiply by that number to get the final result.
Crit chance explanation
With a 25% 'percent chance' to increase damage by 'some percent', this is equivalent to (on average, with some variance) increasing your damage dealt by 25% of your 'some percent' damage increase. * A 25% 'percent chance' to increase damage by 75% is equivalent to increasing your damage by 18.75% (25% of a +75% damage increase is a 1.1875x damage increase)
* A 1% 'percent chance' to increase damage by 75% is equivalent to increasing your damage by 0.75% (1% of a +75% damage increase is a 1.0075x damage increase)
* A 25% 'percent chance' to increase damage by 100% is equivalent to increasing your damage by 25% (25% of a +100% damage increase is a 1.25x increase)
* A 1% 'percent chance' to increase damage by 100% is equivalent to increasing your damage by 1% (1% of a +100% damage increase is a 1.01x increase)

{{cai|Living Battery|Zeri}} against executed targets * {{cai|Satchel Charge|Ziggs}} against turrets below the health threshold * {{ui|Rift Herald|Rift Herald's}} charge against turrets * {{iis|Serpent's Fang}} {{nie|Shield Reaver}} against {{tip|shield|shields}} * {{ri|Arcane Comet}} when dealing damage at 100% increase * {{ri|Demolish}} (incorrectly uses the critical strike icon instead) === Capped damage === == Damage value modifiers == ''See also: [[Damage modifier]]'' === Invulnerability === ''See also: [[Invulnerability]]'' === Calculating mitigation === ''See also: [[Armor]] and [[Magic Resistance]]'' === Calculating applied damage === ''See also: [[Shields]]'' ==Subtypes== ===Resistance subtypes=== ''See also: [[Armor]] and [[Magic Resistance]]'' Resistance subtypes are a secondary typing system that exists to promote [[champion classes]] by diversifying the effectiveness of items and champion match-ups. There is a small selection of effects that are triggered by specific subtypes rather than the above archetypes - e.g. {{ii|Morellonomicon}} will trigger on anything with the {{as|magic damage}} subtype, including abilities, basic attacks and on-hit effects (i.e. {{ii|Wit's End}} will trigger Morellonomicon on a champion with no other source of magic damage). These are the damage types visible to players in-game. {| class="article-table" !Name!!Description!!Example |- |{{tip|Physical damage}}||A damage type thematically associated with making physical contact, such as fists, swords and the physical projectiles of bows and guns. {{sti|Armor}} reduces incoming physical damage.||Most basic attacks; most {{as|AD-scaling}} abilities; some item effects. |- |{{tip|Magic damage}}||A damage type thematically associated with non-physical, such as magic or the supernatural. {{sti|Magic resistance}} reduces incoming magic damage.||Most {{as|AP-scaling}} abilities; some item effects. |- |{{tip|True damage}}||A damage type thematically associated with bypassing the target's defenses. Not to be confused with {{tip|raw damage}}.||A select few sources, such as {{si|Smite}}, {{si|Ignite}}, {{ai|Silver Bolts|Vayne}} and {{ai|Reckless Swing|Olaf}}. |} ==Calculating Damage== : ''Also see: [[Damage modifier]]. The following effects influence damage as non-zero values, in no particular order of calculation. They may originate from the attacker or the target. * Percentage damage amplification * Percentage damage reduction * Flat damage reduction * Resistances, meaning {{stil|armor}} and {{stil|magic resistance}}, against {{as|physical damage}} and {{as|magic damage}}, respectively * Resistances reduction * Resistances penetration, meaning {{stil|armor penetration}} and {{stil|magic penetration}} Resistances effectively reduce the respective damage subtype (physical or magic) by a '''percentage'''. However, '''"percent damage reduction"''' is a different, independent effect: abilities such as {{cai|Unbreakable Will|Alistar}} and item effects such as {{iis|Plated Steelcaps}} ''Plating'' may grant it as a beneficial effect while effects such as {{si|Exhaust}} may apply it as a [[debuff]]. Percent damage modifiers {{tip|stacks multiplicatively|stack multiplicatively}} with the damage reduction achieved through resistances. After the physical and magic damage is affected by the various reductions, it is applied to the target in {{stil|health|health amount}}. This amount received by the target is called ''post-mitigation damage''. ==Capped Damage== Some abilities, scaling with {{as|target's health}}, have a capped amount of damage they can deal to a target. This is made to avoid dealing massive damage to targets with a lot of health, most often against only {{tip|minions}} and/or {{tip|monsters}}. *If the ability deals enough damage (before damage reductions) to reach the cap, the ability's damage is reduced to the cap and damage reductions are then applied. This means that against a target that has negative armor or magic resistance the ability's post-mitigation damage can be higher than the cap. ==Misconceptions== The resistance types—physical, magic and true—are often regarded by players to be the archetypal damage types, which leads to a lot of misconceptions. For example, some players believe that magic damage, ability damage and AP are all interchangeable terms, with even prominent streamers referring to abilities as dealing "AP damage" and "AD damage". This is incorrect. It is possible for basic attacks to deal magic damage (e.g. {{ci|Thresh}} with a point in {{Ai|Flay|Thresh}}); it is possible for abilities to deal physical damage (e.g. {{ci|Riven}}); it is possible for AD-scaling abilities to deal magic damage (e.g. {{ci|Shyvana}}); and it is possible for non-magic damage to apply spell effects (e.g. {{ii|Luden's Echo}} would trigger on Riven if she chose to buy it, although she's discouraged due to her having no AP scalings). Similarly, many players believe that life steal and spell vamp are specific to physical and magic damage, respectively. Life steal will apply to anything classified as basic damage (including the magic damage from {{ai|Takedown|Nidalee}} and {{ai|Infinite Duress|Warwick}} and true damage from {{ai|Hextech Munitions|Corki}}), and spell vamp will apply to anything classified as ability damage (including the physical damage from {{ai|Comet Spear|Pantheon}} and true damage from {{ai|Reckless Swing|Olaf}}). ==See also== *[[Damage modifier]] *[[Magic damage]] *[[Physical damage]] *[[True damage]] {{Gameplay elements}} [[de:Schaden]] [[es:Daño]] [[pl:Obrażenia]] [[ru:Урон]] [[zh:伤害]] [[Category:Gameplay elements]]

Assist
pages.content:
An '''assist''' takes place when an ally has helped a teammate score a [[kill]] on an enemy [[champion]] recently before that enemy's [[death]]. More specifically, within the same duration required for kill credit since the moment that the enemy has died:
* '''15''' seconds, on [[Summoner's Rift]]
* '''20''' seconds, on [[Howling Abyss]]

This timer refreshes upon contributing to the kill again with another valid effect. In addition to damage, there are various other ways to score an assist.

Kills and assists together are called ''[[takedown]]s'', which may be scored to trigger various beneficial effects.

== Assist bounty ==
The [[experience (champion)|experience]] bounty for assisted champion kills is different than the one for scoring a kill alone. An assist [[gold]] bounty is additionally generated when an assist is scored which is equal to half of the champion's dispensed gold bounty, capped at 50% of the '''base''' amount. If an enemy champion is executed by {{cai|Death from Below|Pyke}}, the last assisting ally receives 1 ''{{ii|Your Cut}}'' instead of the assist bounty. ''Your Cut's'' gold is capped at 100% of the '''base''' amount instead.

The slain champion's experience bounty is split equally among all contributors, meaning both the killer and assistors, whereas the assist gold bounty is split equally among assistors. The killer always earns the enemy's full kill gold bounty.

== Direct triggers of assist credit ==
The main effects that are valid for scoring an assist are the same as the ones for being [[Kill#Credit|credited a kill]].

== Indirect triggers of assist credit ==
Champions may also be rewarded with assists without hitting or [[debuff]]ing a slain enemy directly, by:
* Granting a {{tip|heal}}, {{tip|shield}}, or otherwise form of [[buff]] to the killer or another assistor.
* Enclosing the enemy within {{cai|Dark Procession|Yorick}} at any point during its existence.
* Damaging {{cis|Yuumi}} ''{{ai|You and Me!|Yuumi|Anchor}}'' then killing Yuumi, even if Yuumi herself was not affected by the assistor in any way.
* Initiating the channel of {{cai|Hounds' Pursuit|Naafiri}} on a target enemy.
* {{tip|Sight|Revealing}} an enemy who was previously inside Fog of War via {{cai|Hawkshot|Ashe}} or {{cai|Heightened Senses|Quinn}} specifically.
** Any other form of revealing '''cannot''' trigger assists on its own, which includes {{tip|ward}} vision.

== Other forms of assists ==
Similarly to assisted champion kills, the game may feature various mechanics or rules for crediting an assist when killing other types of units. These rules may depend on the game mode.

=== Epic monster objectives ===
Epic monsters have varying ways of crediting assists for their rewards, such as considering the champion's range, death status, or whether they assisted in its takedown.

Within the kill feed, champions are credited an assist next to the killer if they participated in taking down the epic {{tip|monster}} before its aggro was reset. If slain by the ally team, this also counts toward player stats and [[Challenges]].

=== Turrets ===
Champions are awarded their share of local gold from [[turret]]s regardless of range if they are currently alive and have recently damaged it:
* Within the last 10 seconds on [[Summoner's Rift]].
** However, within the kill feed, the assisting players are credited within '''15''' seconds{{bug|2}} of damaging the turret instead; this is cosmetic.
* Within the last 30 seconds on [[Howling Abyss]]

=== Ward tracking ===
[[Ward]]s may be [[basic attack|attacked]] or targeted by certain [[ping]]s to reveal a [[File:Enemy Ward time indicator.png|20px|link=Ward#Ward_Timers|Ward Timer (full)]] [[Ward#Ward_Timers|timer]] to the team, which tracks their remaining duration. The first player to do so is credited {{g|5}}, which is removed from the ward's bounty due to the tracking player being considered as "assisting" with finding the ward and subsequently allowing it to be destroyed.

pages.content:
{{rune header|Triumph}}

== Notes ==
* The healing is calculated based on your missing health at the moment the takedown happened.
** If during the delay another takedown is achieved, all pending '''Triumph''' heals have their calculated value updated to the new amount, which is of course based on your missing health at the moment the latest takedown happened.{{bug|2}}
* A missile with a fixed travel time of 1 seconds handles the delay and functionally triggers the benefits.
** The missile is set as ''unblockable'', which means that it isn't destroyed by colliding with effects such as {{cai|Wind Wall|Yasuo}}.
** The missile can be {{tip|Homing_projectile_destruction|popped}} by effects that (unintentionally) destroy missiles from their own team aimed at them such as {{cai|Trickster|Fizz}}<!--Fizz E2 specifically--> or {{cai|Frozen Tomb|Lissandra}}<!--both of these's missile pops are bugged in this way at the time of this note's creation in late 2023-->. This will prevent both the bonus gold and healing from being received.{{bug}}

== Strategy ==
* '''Triumph''' is often taken in [[ARAM]], as the single lane setup causes regular teamfights leading to a lot of takedowns, thus triggering more times than the average [[Summoner's Rift]] game.
